Span space decomposition is a value-based partitioning strategy that minimizes isosurface extraction time by reorganizing volumetric data into a two-dimensional space defined by field value ranges rather than spatial coordinates [S2].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S2]. The source explicitly states that value-based partitioning approaches minimize isosurface extraction time by reorganizing data into a two-dimensional span space based on field value ranges (minimum and maximum field values), rather than using spatial coordinates. It further details that cells are projected into 2D points defined by these value ranges and that efficiency is achieved through optimized data structures on this span space.
